message.content:
Produce a HEAD-TO-HEAD for the best CANADIAN (ON/BC) acquisition for Hooman at up to ~$500K CAD. He is a Canadian citizen (so BDC/CSBFP/bank financing IS available — unlike US SBA), currently living in the US on TN (green card soon), willing to go full-time. Skills: AI/ML, data eng, cloud/infra, EE, strong diligence.

All categories + real Canadian deals (JSON):
{
  "categories": [
    {
      "category": "SaaS / Software / Apps (Canadian-domiciled)",
      "economics": "Micro/small Canadian B2B SaaS trades ~3–5x SDE (or ~2–4x ARR for clean recurring-revenue businesses; AI/media 'story' listings push to 4x+ revenue). The BizQuest BC staffing SaaS (~4x SDE, ~2.2x revenue) is a fair mid-point comp. A well-bought 4x-SDE SaaS yields ~25% pre-tax owner earnings on purchase price — enough to service a BDC/seller note. Owner-hours are genuinely low for a mature, contractor-supported SaaS (the top pick runs on 5 contractors, home-based); time concentrates in sales/rainmaking, which is the key owner-dependence risk to diligence. Reality: the ≤$500K CAD all-cash tier is dominated by tiny/pre-revenue 2026 'AI app' flips (grocery, restaurant, pet) with no moat; durable recurring-revenue SaaS at ≤$500K all-cash is rare — the good ones sit at $700K–$1.35M and require financing.",
      "financing": "Hooman IS eligible (Canadian citizen). CSBFP: the June 2022 expansion raised the max to $1.15M CAD total, of which up to $500K CAD can now cover equipment, leasehold, INTANGIBLE ASSETS and WORKING CAPITAL — critical because SaaS deals are almost entirely goodwill/intangibles the old CSBFP wouldn't fund (ISED overview confirms coverage now includes 'intellectual property, working capital... and more'; lender fronts loan, gov guarantees ~85%). BDC finances goodwill-heavy acquisitions on cash-flow underwriting, typically expecting ~10–25% buyer equity down and often pairing a term loan with a seller note; BDC is more comfortable than a chartered bank with intangible/cash-flow-based SaaS. Practical structure for the ~$1.35M top pick: ~$400–500K CAD Hooman equity + BDC/bank term loan + seller note (seller financing offered) — keeps it inside his cash while acquiring a >$500K asset. Canadian specifics: register GST/HST (SaaS is taxable supply); no provincial trade-license for pure software EXCEPT regulated verticals (the lending listing = money-services/consumer-lending licensing; payroll/HR SaaS touches remittance compliance). Watch USD-vs-CAD pricing — the top deal is quoted in USD. (BDC 'buy a business' hub 404'd at fetch time; confirm live equity % with a BDC account manager — 10–25% + seller-note is the standard norm.)",
      "remote": "Best category in the entire Canadian search for remote operation. Every listing is software and operable from the US on TN status; several are explicitly 'home-based / relocatable / remote.' No Canadian physical presence needed to RUN them. Caveats: the entity must stay Canadian-domiciled (ON/BC incorporation) to unlock BDC/CSBFP even while operated remotely; listings with employees (cybersecurity SaaS: 6 staff) are less solo-remote than contractor-run ones (staffing SaaS: 5 contractors). TN restricts operating a US business, not owning/managing a Canadian company remotely — so this category sidesteps the immigration constraint cleanly.",
      "fit": "Extremely high. His AI/ML + data-engineering + cloud/infra + EE + diligence stack is the exact toolkit to underwrite these better than a generalist buyer, personally modernize a 16-year-old codebase or a thin 'AI' product, cut infra cost and add defensible AI features post-close, and run it remotely without hiring. Weakness (shared by any solo software acquirer): sales/rainmaking is the owner-dependence risk in most of these — especially the staffing SaaS — and he has no sales track record, so factor a sales hire or a strong transition period into diligence.",
      "verdict": "STRONG BUY category — the best-fit and most remote-operable of the whole Canadian search — but the true sub-$500K all-cash shelf is thin. The genuinely durable, cash-flowing Canadian SaaS (BizQuest 16-yr BC staffing platform: <2% churn, 55% margin, ~4x SDE, ~$338K CAD SDE) sits at ~$1.35M CAD and is a finance-with-BDC/seller-note deal, not all-cash; the all-cash ≤$500K tier is dominated by 2026 'AI app' flips with no moat (skip). Recommended play: target one proven, low-churn vertical B2B SaaS in the $700K–$1.35M range, put ~$400–500K CAD down, and lever the rest with BDC + seller paper — using Canadian citizenship for the financing he can't get in the US. Lead candidate: #1 BC Staffing-Mgmt SaaS; watch #2 Quebec SaaS (if near $500K) and #4 Ontario cybersecurity SaaS (if priced modestly) as closer-to-all-cash alternatives. Note: Flippa/Acquire.com/DealStream detail pages were 403/JS-blocked via WebFetch — a manual browser pass is needed to fully sweep the true ≤$500K all-cash micro-SaaS band.",
      "deal_count": 8
    },
    {
      "category": "E-commerce / DTC brands (Canadian)",
      "economics": "Small Canadian DTC/e-com brands under ~$500K trade 2.5x-4x SDE; higher-quality (strong repeat %, trademark, clean books, >30% margin) reaches 4x-4.5x (Vancouver beauty brand ~4.2x). Inventory is frequently bundled into the headline asking price (Calgary and furniture deals are almost entirely working capital), inflating effective multiples — always separate enterprise value from stock. Margins: personal-care/beauty consumables run 25-35% SDE margin; inventory-heavy general e-com/furniture/apparel run thin 4-10% and are working-capital traps. At 3-4x SDE, unlevered pre-tax yield is ~25-40% of price, but real take-home drops once you pay a fulfillment operator you're replacing. Owner hours 20-40/wk; the binding constraint is almost always physical manufacture/fulfillment, not the storefront. Moat quality: subscription/Subscribe-&-Save recurring > trademarked own-formula consumable > multi-channel branded goods > single-marketplace reseller > dropship (avoid).",
      "financing": "CSBFP is largely UNUSABLE here: it finances equipment, leasehold improvements, and real property — NOT goodwill, inventory, or share purchases, which is exactly what a DTC brand acquisition consists of. BDC does small-business acquisition/transition financing (the more relevant lender) but expects 20-35% buyer equity down, a personal guarantee, and discounts goodwill heavily; pure-goodwill DTC brands with little equipment are hard to lever, so most sub-$500K DTC deals are done mostly cash + seller note. Seller notes are common/available on several of these listings (deodorant, smart-home, staffing SaaS) — typically 10-25% of price over 2-4 yrs — and are the single best leverage source. Non-resident friction: Hooman is a Canadian citizen (no immigration bar to own/operate), but a US address/banking history complicates BDC underwriting — cleanest terms likely need Canadian personal banking history or relocation. Use the GST/HST s.167 going-concern election on asset deals to avoid GST on the transfer.",
      "remote": "Honest verdict: most Canadian DTC brands are NOT truly remote because the moat (own-brand consumable) is tied to physical manufacture/fulfillment in Canada. REMOTE: only the Smart-Home E-com+SaaS deal (app + cloud subscriptions; e-com paused) is genuinely laptop-runnable from the US — and it happens to be the best founder-fit, though it's a turnaround. SEMI-ABSENTEE: deodorant, beauty, furniture, HelloDough — marketable/sellable remotely but each needs a Canada-based maker/3PL for production and shipping; runnable from the US only if an operator or co-packer is retained. ON-SITE-REQUIRED: Calgary general e-com, apparel, building-supply — warehouse + staff + inventory demand ground presence in Canada. Until Hooman relocates, practical options from the US are the deodorant/beauty brands (with a retained operator) or the SaaS-flavored deal.",
      "fit": "Weak-to-moderate fit. Hooman's AI/ML/data/cloud/EE edge adds little to a deodorant or furniture brand beyond better ads/analytics — the category under-utilizes his strengths. The only deal that rewards his profile is the Smart-Home E-com + SaaS (proprietary app + cloud subscriptions he could re-architect and scale), but its UK-market focus, hardware dependency, and stalled e-commerce make it a rebuild, not a cash cow. His diligence alpha does apply strongly: multiple listings hide SDE/revenue (furniture, HelloDough) or bundle large inventory into price (Calgary, furniture), so his rigor is what avoids overpaying for working capital dressed as goodwill. The remote constraint bites hardest in this category — DTC brands are physical-product ops, so from the US only the semi-absentee consumables (with a retained operator) or the SaaS-flavored deal are practical.",
      "verdict": "MODERATE — cautiously positive but not the top category for this founder. Canadian sub-$500K DTC brands exist, are cheap (2.5-4x SDE), and several offer seller financing; a couple are genuinely good businesses. Standout best-fit-for-budget: the Central-Ontario natural-deodorant brand ($349K / $100K SDE, 13 yrs, 1,000+ Amazon Subscribe & Save recurring, retirement seller, seller financing, all-cash-affordable) — buy it with a contract co-packer + 3PL installed so it runs semi-absentee while Hooman is US-based. Caveats dragging the category down: (1) the moat is a physical consumable, so it's semi-absentee at best from the US, not remote; (2) the category barely uses Hooman's AI/data edge; (3) CSBFP won't finance goodwill and BDC discounts it, so leverage is limited — mostly cash+seller-note deals; (4) inventory-bundled pricing and gated financials demand heavy diligence. The Smart-Home SaaS+e-com is the only truly-remote/founder-fit option but is a turnaround. Note: businessesforsale.com/canada, Flippa, Empire Flippers and Acquire.com block automated scraping and hide seller location pre-account, so additional Canadian FBA/DTC inventory almost certainly exists there and warrants a manual/account-based pass.",
      "deal_count": 7
    },
    {
      "category": "Content / Media / Newsletters / Communities (Canada)",
      "economics": "BizBuySell median asking for Canadian \"Communication & Media\" is $1,174,500 (range ~$512K to >$1.725M), but that pool is dominated by agencies, print/newspaper, signage, telecom-resellers, and A/V production - NOT durable first-party audience assets. Multiples: content/audience assets (newsletters, ad/affiliate sites) ~2.5-4x SDE, with niche display-ad/affiliate sites trading ~25-40x MONTHLY profit on Flippa/Motion Invest (~2-3.3x annual) and heavily AI-Overview exposed; creative-service agencies ~2.5-4x SDE but low durability; print/newspaper ~1.5-3x and declining. Owner-hours: content/newsletter assets = low and remote; agencies/studios/newspapers = high, on-site, owner-is-the-product. At <=$500K CAD you realistically get either a small services agency ($100-300K SDE, low durability) or a small content/newsletter site ($50-200K SDE at 2.5-4x) bought off Flippa/Acquire - and most of the latter are not Canadian-domiciled.",
      "financing": "CSBFP generally does NOT finance business-acquisition goodwill (it funds equipment/real property/leaseholds), so it is largely inapplicable to content/media/agency buys that are almost pure goodwill + IP - verify per lender. BDC is the realistic lever and does acquisition financing but typically wants 25-35% buyer equity plus a transition plan; pure content/audience assets with no hard assets and lumpy sponsorship revenue are HARD to lever - banks/BDC discount goodwill-only deals heavily (the Vancouver platform with 2 staff and campaign revenue would likely need a large seller note + Hooman equity rather than clean BDC term debt). Service agencies with recurring gov/corporate contracts finance better. Seller financing is available on several listings (Vancouver platform, Red Deer paper, RE-media franchise) and is the most realistic route to a $2M+ platform on $500K cash (~$500K down + large seller note). HST: business asset sales are commonly done under the s.167 going-concern election (no HST on transfer) - handle in the purchase agreement.",
      "remote": "Split. Content/newsletter/audience assets (the Vancouver Clean Energy Media Platform) are fully REMOTE and explicitly relocatable - runnable from the US today. Everything else in the ON/BC media pool (video-production agency, recording studio, local newspaper, RE-media franchise) is SEMI-ABSENTEE-to-ON-SITE because it needs people/crew/facilities on the ground in Canada. Important caveat: the most remote-runnable content assets are also the least tied to Canada (global audience, location-agnostic USD-ish ad/affiliate revenue), so a content site with merely a Canadian seller may not deliver the Canadian-domicile financing/immigration benefit the mandate is built around; the clean-energy platform is the exception because it's an actual BC-registered operating company with a real owned email list.",
      "fit": "Only partial fit. Content/media value is audience + editorial + sponsor relationships, not AI/ML/data engineering - Hooman would be buying a business whose core competency isn't his. His diligence edge and ability to bolt on automation (AI content ops, programmatic SEO, market-intelligence/lead-gen data products) is real but secondary. AI-Overview/LLM answer engines are the dominant durability threat, compressing top-of-funnel traffic to ad/affiliate content; the defensible sub-asset is an owned email list/community (first-party, algorithm-independent) - which is why the Vancouver deal's 50K-subscriber list matters more than its pageviews. Best-fit play is a content business with a durable first-party channel where his data/automation skills add value, conceptually the clean-energy platform, though its price and vertical concentration undercut it.",
      "verdict": "WEAK-to-MODERATE fit; do not prioritize as the primary acquisition. The Canadian content/media market at <=$500K CAD is dominated by declining print, on-site creative-service agencies, and franchise photography - none durable, remote, and founder-fit. The genuinely attractive profile (durable first-party audience, remote, high margin) is rare; the one strong example, the Vancouver Clean Energy Media Platform, is ~$2.4M at ~10x EBITDA, revenue-lumpy, vertically concentrated, and goodwill-only (hard for BDC to lever, a stretch even with heavy seller financing on $500K cash). Content assets are also the most exposed to AI-Overview/SEO decay and least aligned with the Canadian-domicile financing/immigration thesis. If pursued anyway: (1) negotiate the Vancouver platform down with a heavy seller note and add AI/data products where Hooman's skills create value, or (2) buy a smaller $100-300K content/newsletter asset off Flippa/Acquire as a cash-flowing secondary, accepting it likely won't be Canadian-domiciled. Otherwise route the primary $500K to a category with hard cash flow BDC will lever and clearer founder-fit.",
      "deal_count": 5
    },
    {
      "category": "Local service businesses (ON/BC home & trades)",
      "economics": "Owner-operator ON/BC home-service shops trade ~1.5x-3.3x SDE; sub-$500K deals cluster ~2-3x SDE. Larger institutionalized contractors (Sudbury $2.2M/$490K SDE, Barrie $3.5M/$800K CF, Okanagan $2.59M/$544K EBITDA) push 3-4x SDE/EBITDA. At ~2.5-3x SDE, unlevered SDE yield is ~33-40% of price BEFORE debt service and BEFORE paying a GM to replace the owner (mandatory here given remote constraint) — a $90-120K GM eats 40-60% of SDE on the smaller deals. SDE/revenue margins ranged ~11% (fence, sub-heavy) to ~35% (HVAC GTA) to ~29% (cleaning). Owner-hours are high full-time (dispatch, quoting, crew/sub management, seasonal swings) for HVAC/plumbing/cleaning/fencing; the low-voltage integrator and painting/detailing franchises are the most 'manage-a-team' (least tools-in-hand). Durability driver = recurring maintenance/route revenue (HVAC maintenance, cleaning, exterior detailing). HST/GST+PST (13% ON, 5%+7% BC) affects working capital and revenue verification.",
      "financing": "The Canadian financing edge is real for a Canadian citizen. BDC is the go-to acquisition lender, more flexible than chartered banks and can finance a higher % than conventional lenders (which want 20-35% equity down per CFIB/broker sources); no zero-down acquisition loans exist in Canada. CSBFP: max $1.15M/borrower, eligible businesses <=$10M gross revenue (all these qualify), BUT it finances HARD ASSETS ONLY — equipment+leasehold up to $500K combined, intangibles up to $150K, working-capital LOC up to $150K — and CRITICALLY does NOT finance goodwill or share purchases. Since most of a home-service purchase price is goodwill/blue-sky (customer base, routes, brand), CSBFP realistically only covers the trucks/equipment portion; the practical stack is BDC + chartered-bank term loan + seller VTB, with CSBFP layered onto equipment. Seller VTBs appear in these listings (low-voltage integrator 20-30% down/3-5yr; London cleaning VTB), so ~$500K cash comfortably covers a 20-30% down + BDC/bank + 10-25% VTB structure. Asset sales (most listings) avoid hidden liabilities but forfeit any goodwill financing.",
      "remote": "Weakest category for Hooman's current US residency. Home-service/trades are physically rooted: local crews, trucks, dispatch, same-day/emergency response, in-market sales, and provincially LICENSED trades. None can be run from a laptop in the US. ON-SITE-REQUIRED: HVAC (GTA/Southern ON/Okanagan), plumbing, cleaning, fencing, restoration. SEMI-ABSENTEE (best available): the Richmond low-voltage integrator (retained Office Mgr + Technical Lead), painting franchise (crew-lead model), exterior detailing franchise — but even these need frequent on-the-ground presence and a trusted #2. Trade-licensing blocker: ON gas = TSSA G1/G2 + ODP, electrical = ECRA/ESA + 309A CofQ; BC = Technical Safety BC permits, compulsory-certified plumbing/gas/electrical. Hooman (EE degree, not a Red-Seal tradesperson) CANNOT hold these licenses himself and must retain the licensed key-man — the single biggest operational risk in every trades deal. Feasible only if he relocates to Canada or installs a strong licensed local GM before closing.",
      "fit": "Skills fit is mostly indirect — AI/ML/data/cloud/EE + diligence doesn't run a plumbing truck. Where it helps: (a) the Richmond low-voltage integrator is a genuine EE/electronics adjacency and already ships 'AI proposal automation' he could extend; (b) diligence alpha on the anomalously cheap Toronto fence business (~1.5x SDE) and the SDE-gated Okanagan plumbing deal; (c) value-creation by layering software/routing/CRM/AI-scheduling onto any acquisition. The binding constraint is immigration/geography, not skills: Canadian citizen (financing unlocked) but US-resident (operations locked) — this category is exactly where that tension bites hardest, making him an absentee cross-border owner of a hands-on business on day one.",
      "verdict": "MEDIOCRE FIT — not recommended as the #1 acquisition while Hooman lives in the US. Economics are attractive (2-3x SDE, 30-40% unlevered yields, BDC/VTB financing genuinely available to a Canadian citizen), but every deal is physically on-the-ground and most trades require a license Hooman doesn't hold, so he'd be an absentee cross-border owner on day one — the worst posture for a hands-on service business. If pursued anyway, ranked shortlist: (1) Richmond low-voltage integrator $389K — best founder-fit (EE/AI adjacency, existing AI automation), retained team, 20-30% down seller financing, semi-absentee-plausible; diligence the technical-lead key-man risk and verify $130K SDE. (2) CertaPro painting franchise St. Catharines $385K (~2.1x SDE) — crew-manage model, franchisor scaffolding. (3) Toronto fence $559K — only if diligence explains the ~1.5x SDE and the 11% margin isn't a mirage. Treat this whole category as a RELOCATION-CONTINGENT option; revisit seriously once Hooman is in Canada. Until then favour remote-runnable software/SaaS acquisitions.",
      "deal_count": 8
    },
    {
      "category": "Physical / real-asset businesses (ON/BC): laundromats, self-storage, car washes, vending routes",
      "economics": "Laundromats (leasehold) are the only tier that fits sub-$500K all-cash: metro ON/BC coin stores run ~$120K-$350K/yr revenue, rent $35K-$85K/yr, utilities (gas+water+hydro) 20-35% of revenue, near-zero labor if unattended. Realistic SDE $40K-$120K; leasehold multiples ~2.5-3.5x SDE (higher if unattended/card-enabled with a long lease). All-cash yield on a $300-450K buy is ~15-30% pre-tax IF disclosed revenue is real — but net income is essentially never published, and utility inflation is the killer variable. Car washes split into self-serve leaseholds ($345-450K, ~2.5-3x SDE) and express-tunnel-with-real-estate ($1.5M-$12M, sold on 6-8% cap, 40-55% EBITDA but far over budget). Self-storage has the best economics (80%+ gross margin, minimal labor, sticky inflation-linked rents, cap rates 5.5-8%) but no going-concern facility is buyable at $500K all-cash in ON/BC — it's a $2M-$10M+ / raise-or-build play. Vending is lowest barrier/lowest reward ($10-30K SDE per small route). Owner-hours: unattended card laundromat 5-15/wk; attended/wash-&-fold 30+/wk; vending weekly local restock.",
      "financing": "Canadian leverage is genuinely available (unlike US SBA for a TN holder). CSBFP finances equipment + leasehold improvements (fits washers/dryers, car-wash gear) with an 85% guarantee, up to ~$500K equipment/leaseholds, typically ~10-25% buyer equity — BUT CSBFP does NOT finance goodwill, a real problem for leasehold laundromat deals where much of the price is goodwill. BDC does acquisition/business-transfer financing, favors hard assets/real estate, and often pairs a term/real-estate loan with working capital; for a $300-450K laundromat expect ~20-35% down. So $500K cash buys ONE solid laundromat outright (best asset utilization, keep a cash buffer for utility spikes/equipment) OR serves as down payment on a ~$1.2-1.6M car-wash/small-storage-with-real-estate, where land collateral unlocks a commercial mortgage + BDC top-up — turning $500K into a leveraged, appreciating, amortizing asset. Provincial specifics: HST 13% ON / GST+PST 12% BC; use the s.167 GST/HST election on asset sales to avoid tax on transfer; municipal business licensing; car washes need MECP/environmental & effluent permits and may carry soil-contamination liability (Hamilton listing showed $534K remediation/capex); laundromats need gas/utility + fire-code sign-off.",
      "remote": "Weak overall for a US-resident owner. The ONLY genuinely semi-absentee option is an unattended, card/app-enabled laundromat (machines report online; hire a local cleaner + on-call technician) — this is also where Hooman's data/cloud skills add value (app-pay, dynamic pricing, remote monitoring), but it still needs a trusted local contractor, so SEMI-ABSENTEE at best, never fully remote. Attended laundromats/wash-&-fold are ON-SITE-REQUIRED. Self-serve car washes are SEMI-ABSENTEE only with a reliable local manager (breakdowns, cash handling, weather, compliance), else ON-SITE. Self-storage would be the most remote-friendly (online rentals, remote gate) but isn't buyable at this budget. Vending is ON-SITE-REQUIRED (weekly restocking) and the worst remote fit. Bottom line: from the US, only an unattended card-based laundromat is realistically runnable; everything else pushes toward relocation or a hired GM that eats the thin margins.",
      "fit": "Below-average fit. His diligence-alpha is genuinely valuable here because sellers hide net income (revenue disclosed, SDE almost never) — verifying payment-processor and utility records is exactly the edge that separates a good laundromat buy from a bad one. His cloud/data/EE skills map onto converting a store to unattended card/app operation and remote monitoring. BUT the category's core realities — physical presence, thin utility-exposed margins, local trade licensing/environmental compliance, and low SDE at the affordable tier — cut against a remote US-based AI/software founder. This ranks below the digital/software acquisition categories for him. Worth exactly ONE serious swing (an unattended, long-lease Toronto/Vancouver laundromat ≤$450K, or a leveraged car-wash/storage-with-real-estate) if he specifically wants a tangible, financeable, inflation-hedged cash asset; otherwise deprioritize.",
      "verdict": "Asset-backed and financeable, but a weak founder-fit and weak remote-fit for Hooman right now. Deals that fit $500K all-cash (leasehold laundromats, self-serve car-wash leaseholds, vending) are low-SDE, financially opaque, utility-inflation-exposed, and mostly require local presence — the exact constraints that hurt a US-resident AI/data engineer most. The genuinely attractive assets (express car washes, self-storage) have great low-labor cash flow but sit at $1.5M-$10M and need real leverage plus relocation or a hired operator. Recommended shape if pursued: (1) best all-cash pick = a metro unattended, card/app-enabled laundromat with a long lease priced ≤$450K, where his tech edge and the only real remote-operability live — diligence must VERIFY coin/app revenue and lease term; (2) best leverage pick = a car-wash/small-storage WITH real estate (~$1.2-1.6M) using $400-500K down + BDC/commercial mortgage, trading remote-operability for a better appreciating asset. Overall: worth one serious laundromat swing, but this category ranks BELOW the software/online acquisition categories for a remote US-based AI founder.",
      "deal_count": 6

    {
      "category": "B2B distribution / niche manufacturing / light industrial (ON & BC)",
      "economics": "Canadian sub-$1M-SDE deals in this category trade at honest, often cheap multiples: owner-operator trades/service (GC, HVAC, electromechanical) ~2.0–3.0x SDE (cheap because cash flow is largely the owner's own labour and transfers poorly); niche/precision manufacturing & machine shops ~2.5–3.5x SDE (the Precision-Machined listing at 4.8x is above market); specialty distribution/wholesale ~2.5–4x SDE but working-capital-heavy so effective cash needed exceeds the multiple; recurring-revenue B2B services (service contracts/maintenance) 3–4x+ deservedly. Owner-hours: trades/GC/HVAC are typically full-time on-site owner-operator (45–60 hrs/wk); distribution can be semi-absentee with an ops manager. Unlevered cash-on-cash yield looks like 30–50% at 2–3x SDE, but much of that \"yield\" is really a salary for a job you must show up to. Durability is a genuine strength — physical fabrication, motor repair, HVAC service and GC are AI-safe and not disruption-prone — but none are software-scalable and all are skilled-labour/license-gated.",
      "financing": "Verified from bdc.ca: BDC business-acquisition financing explicitly funds goodwill, IP and client lists, refinances vendor notes, offers cash-flow-matched repayment; requires Canadian-based, revenue-generating, good credit; no published fixed down-payment (practically ~20–35% equity for these sizes, and BDC often co-lends alongside a chartered bank rather than 100%). CSBFP (Canada Small Business Financing Program) is government-backed but lends only against equipment, real property and leasehold improvements — NOT goodwill or share purchases — capped at $1.15M total (up to $500K equipment/leaseholds); a goodwill-heavy service deal needs CSBFP paired with a BDC/bank term loan for the goodwill. Seller financing (VTB) is common here — the BC GC (#44625001) and Electromechanical (#54714002) both advertise it; 10–30% VTB is normal and de-risks lender approval. Practical structure for a ~$500K deal: ~$100–175K cash down + BDC/bank 5–10yr term loan + 10–25% seller VTB, which reaches the ~$700K–$1M band, making the HVAC ($1.1M) and a negotiated Precision-Machined ($880K) financeable despite exceeding $500K all-cash. Canadian specifics: HST registration (~13% ON / 5% GST + PST BC); trade licensing (ON TSSA G2/313A for gas/HVAC, ESA electrical, PEO C-of-A for engineering; BC Red Seal/TQ, WorkSafeBC, GC bonding); asset-vs-share purchase changes tax treatment; lenders typically want a Canadian-resident director/manager.",
      "remote": "Worst-fit category for Hooman's US-residency constraint. In-budget, effectively NONE are remotely runnable from the US. ON-SITE-REQUIRED: Precision-Machined (#54128004), BC GC (#44625001), Electromechanical (#54714002), Consulting Engineering (#44625005) — shop floor, subs, client visits, licensed work. SEMI-ABSENTEE only with a strong retained GM: Bedding Wholesaler (#44717006), Skincare mfr (#54509001), and (far over budget) the $6.2M Management-Led Exterior Construction firm. Even the semi-absentee ones need a trusted on-ground manager plus periodic in-person presence, and few BDC/bank lenders will underwrite a first-time, out-of-country operator running a manager-only business. Realistically Hooman must relocate to ON/BC or hire (and pay for) a GM day one, which eats the SDE that made these deals cheap.",
      "fit": "Partial. His EE background is genuinely relevant to the Electromechanical motor/transformer shop and the MEP Consulting Engineering firm, and his data/AI/automation skills could modernize a distributor (forecasting, pricing, e-comm) or a machine shop's quoting/ops; his diligence is a real asset in this opaque, financials-gated marketplace.
